title: Finite compact-flat subcomplex diagrams
statement: Let Y be a scheme and A its category of module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Let L_n be a bounded-above tower of cochain complexes, with degreewise split monic transitions l_n. Suppose every L_n^i is a coproduct of flat module sheaves [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] G_j, each coproduct-compact: every map from G_j to a small coproduct factors through a finite subcoproduct. There exist a small preorder I, a monotone stage map sigma:I→N, and a functor D:I→CoCh(A), with the following properties. I_n={j|sigma(j)≤n} is filtered and nonempty. For every n there is a specified cocone D|I_n→L_n which is a colimit, all of whose components are degreewise monic. For j∈I_n these cocones commute strictly with l_n. Every D(j) vanishes outside a finite interval of integer degrees. For every n the upper bounds of D(j), j∈I_n, have a common bound. Every D(j)^i is a finite coproduct of coproduct-compact flat sheaves, with the same finite-subcoproduct factorization property. No target telescope or bar complex is involved.

source.place: the finite-subcomplex paragraph beginning “Fix generator decompositions in each term”.

proof.text: Fix the actual generator families and coproduct isomorphisms supplied by hgen. For each generator choose a finite support for its differential. Truncate successor supports at a chosen upper bound b: the differential into every higher term is zero. The private finite_closed_support lemma, proved by strong induction on (b - degree + 1).toNat, closes every finite set of degree-labelled generators under these successor supports. Form each term as its literal finite subcoproduct. Its inclusion is monic by Mathlib MonoCoprod.mono_of_injective'. Restrict the differential by its uniquely determined factor through the next inclusion. Cancellation of that inclusion proves d squared is zero and constructs the inclusion chain map. The finite set of labelled generators bounds the nonzero degrees.

For a chain map from any such finite piece to another stage, apply coproduct compactness to each of its finitely many generator summands, unite the finitely many supports and close that union under the target differential. This constructs a degreewise factor through one target finite piece. Cancellation of its monic inclusion proves that the factor is a chain map. This is the fully proved private factor_through_stable_piece lemma; no additional theorem with sorry is used.

Index by the small type of triples (stage, finite degree-labelled support, proof of differential stability). Order two triples when the first stage is at most the second and the iterated tower transition carries its inclusion through the second finite piece. Identity and composition give a preorder. Factors are unique by monicity, so they define a functor. Form each stage augmentation by composing the piece inclusion with Functor.ofSequence applied to the tower. Functoriality gives naturality and strict compatibility. Carry two pieces to stage n, apply the previous factorization construction, unite the resulting supports and close them. This gives a common upper object at stage n, and hence filteredness of the initial-stage preorder. Closing the empty support supplies an object even for the zero tower.

Every generator of every term of L_n lies in a finite piece labelled n by closing its singleton support. Thus the supremum of the degreewise images of the stage-n augmentations is top: factor the coproduct inverse isomorphism through that supremum using Sigma.desc. The proved source library subobjectEval_iSup and subobjectEval_injective identify the supremum of the corresponding subobjects of the complex with top. SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian supplies the Grothendieck abelian structure, inherited by cochain complexes. Apply Mathlib IsGrothendieckAbelian.isColimitMapCoconeOfSubobjectMkEqISup to this filtered diagram of monomorphisms into L_n. It proves exactly the required colimit cocone.

The augmentation maps are degreewise monic because finite subcoproduct inclusions and all composites of the given split monic tower transitions are monic. The upper bound of L_n itself bounds every piece appearing by stage n, by IsZero.of_mono; no maximum of bounds from earlier stages is needed. Each term is the actual finite subcoproduct of the original generators, and flatness and the coproduct-compact factorization property are inherited directly from hgen. Assemble these proved fields into CompactFlatFiniteSubcomplexDiagrams. The original theorem has no remaining sorry and its axioms are exactly propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

proof_origin.place: The finite-subcomplex paragraph, implemented directly by finite support closure and the existing Mathlib filtered-subobject colimit theorem; every private helper is proved.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_compact_flat_finite_subcomplex_diagrams (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (L : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (l : ∀ n : ℕ, L n ⟶ L (n + 1))
    (hb : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ z : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, z < i → IsZero ((L n).X i))
    (hsplit : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), IsSplitMono ((l n).f i))
    (hgen :
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), ∃ (I : Type u)
        (G : I → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)),
        Nonempty ((L n).X i ≅ ∐ G) ∧
        (∀ j : I, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (G j)) ∧
        ∀ (j : I) (K : Type u)
          (H : K → SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))
          (f : G j ⟶ ∐ H),
          ∃ (S : Finset K) (g : G j ⟶ ∐ (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ H k.1)),
            g ≫ Sigma.desc (fun k : {k // k ∈ S} ↦ Sigma.ι H k.1) = f)
 :
    Nonempty (CompactFlatFiniteSubcomplexDiagrams Y L l)
